name: Request an ID or credential from a wallet (verifier)
plain: Asks the phone's wallet for a verified age, name or license, with the person's consent.
meaning: Shares only chosen attributes (age over 21, name, address) cryptographically signed by an issuer. Replaces ID photos and upload flows when it works.

android.permission: None; verifier registration with Google Wallet for production
android.prompt_ui: Credential Manager sheet listing wallet credentials; user approves attributes
android.api_surface: Credential Manager DigitalCredential (androidx.credentials 1.5), OpenID4VP, ISO 18013-7, W3C Digital Credentials API in Chrome
android.note: Android supports mdoc and SD-JWT VC through registry providers; Wallet is one provider.

ios.prompt_ui: Wallet sheet: choose attributes, Face ID
ios.store_policy: Apple entitlement request via Account Holder; verifier agreement
ios.api_surface: IdentityDocumentServices (Verify with Wallet), ProximityReader mobile document reader, Safari W3C Digital Credentials API (iOS 26)
ios.note: iOS 26.1 adds passport based Digital ID; iOS 26.2 adds usageDescription for tailored consent.

limits.headline: Can ask your wallet to prove one fact, such as your age, once you approve
limits.user_action: You tap Verify my age or Verify my ID and approve the wallet prompt
can: Ask the wallet for a specific item, such as over 21, your name, or your license
Receive a signed answer after you approve in the wallet
Use the proof to unlock an age gated or ID gated action
Accept the proof on a web page through the browser
cannot: Receive anything you decline on the wallet screen
See credentials you never added to a wallet
Keep asking for new proofs without a new prompt each time
limits.differs: Android works through Credential Manager and registered wallets. iPhone needs an Apple entitlement and uses Verify with Wallet.

story.what_it_is: An app asks your wallet to prove one fact about you, like your age, instead of uploading an ID photo.

marketing.name: Digital Credentials API
marketing.pitch: Android lets apps and sites request verified details from a wallet, with a clear consent screen.

marketing.name: Verify with Wallet
marketing.pitch: Apple lets apps ask for age or ID details from Wallet and shows what is being shared first.

story.for_you: You see a sheet that says which facts the app wants, like 'over 21' or your name. You approve with Face ID or a fingerprint and nothing else is shared. No photo of your license is needed.
story.for_makers: Makers get a signed fact from the government issuer, so there is less fraud and less ID data stored to protect. It cuts drop offs from long upload steps. They must request only the facts they need, or regulators and users push back.

use_cases.example: An online liquor store asks if you are over 21 and your wallet answers yes without showing your birth date.
A hotel app lets you share your name and ID for check in before you arrive, so you skip the desk.
A bank opens an account in minutes by taking verified name and address from your wallet.
A game with mature content checks your age band once instead of trusting a checkbox.
A social site proves a new user is an adult before it shows age limited rooms.
A car rental or ride app confirms a valid license from your wallet before it unlocks a car.

story.android_note: Android shows a system picker that lists the wallets that can answer the request.
story.ios_note: iPhone shows its own sheet with the exact attributes and requires Face ID, with state support rolling out slowly.

technical_bounds: Verifier must be vetted; credentials issued by supported states and countries only

history.change: Verify with Wallet in apps and web
